posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
I didn't like Kingkiller at all. The main character is too dang competent at individual activities, which is what keeps saving him from his really bad overall decisions. Meanwhile, the framing device with everything happening in the past kept making me yell "no go back to the present THERE IS A CRISIS THERE!" Also, urgh, the faerie bit.

I'll go ahead and stick my neck out again: while I loved "Heir to the Empire" in middle school, when I reread them as an adult I realized that all of Thrawn's "tactical genius" consisted of him revealing a plot-device technology that was previously unknown in the entire Star Wars universe, thus surprising everybody. Is the new version any better written?

Speaking of authors improving, though, I enjoyed the crap out of "The Collapsing Empire." It definitely read like a much more mature Scalzi, without sacrificing any of his fast-paced style.
